text: Adapting large language models under strict hardware limits requires balancing model parameters, optimizer states, gradient graphs, and activations.
This research note evaluates six parameter-efficient methods: LoRA, DoRA, AdaLoRA, QLoRA, LoftQ, and QA-LoRA.

We separate measured results from design choices, analyze memory trade-offs across scales, provide a structured comparison table, specify a controlled single-GPU experimental protocol, and examine critical methodological boundaries, including an unverified laboratory claim.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: Full fine-tuning of large models is computationally prohibitive under tight memory constraints, as optimizers like Adam require 16 bytes per parameter for gradient and momentum tracking.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) mitigates this overhead by freezing pre-trained weights W0 and parameterizing updates as W = r B A, where B Rd × r and A Rr × k with r (d, k).

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: LoRA reduces GPU memory consumption during training by freezing the pre-trained weights and optimizing injected low-rank matrices without storing optimizer states or gradients for the frozen parameters.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: Compared to full fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B, LoRA reduces the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: On GPT-3 175B, LoRA reduces training VRAM consumption from 1.2TB to 350GB when adapting query and value projection matrices with rank r=4.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: While LoRA couples directional and magnitude updates within its low-rank product, Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) analyzes their distinct learning dynamics.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: DoRA decomposes pre-trained weights into magnitude and directional components and applies LoRA to update the directional component.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: DoRA enhances both the learning capacity and training stability of LoRA while avoiding additional inference overhead.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: Backpropagation through column-normalized directions introduces intermediate activations.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: The proposed modification to DoRA leads to a training memory reduction of approximately 24.4% in fine-tuning LLaMA.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: Rather than enforcing a static rank across all layers, Adaptive Budget Allocation (AdaLoRA) dynamically shifts parameter capacity toward modules that most influence task loss.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: AdaLoRA parameterizes incremental updates in the form of singular value decomposition and prunes redundant singular values based on importance scoring.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: To avoid expensive numerical SVD during training, AdaLoRA parameterizes incremental updates to mimic singular value decomposition and adds an orthogonality penalty to regularize singular vectors.

section: Architectural Foundations: Decomposition and Dynamic Allocation
text: Singular values are pruned along a cubic schedule, concentrating capacity in critical layers.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Although adapters eliminate optimizer overhead, storing 16-bit base weights remains memory-intensive (~130 GB for 65B models).

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: QLoRA breaks this barrier by compressing the static backbone into 4-bit representation.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: QLoRA reduces memory usage to enable fine-tuning a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU by combining 4-bit NormalFloat quantization, Double Quantization, and Paged Optimizers.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: QLoRA has one low-precision storage data type in 4-bit and one computation data type in 16-bit BrainFloat.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Weights are dequantized on the fly during computation, while gradients accumulate for 16-bit adapters.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Double Quantization compresses the first-stage quantization constants to save an average of approximately 0.37 bits per parameter.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Paged Optimizers leverage unified memory to mitigate gradient checkpointing memory spikes.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Standard QLoRA quantizes base weights independently while initializing adapters near zero, inducing severe discrepancy in low-bit regimes.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: LoftQ mitigates this issue by treating low-rank adaptation and quantization as a joint objective.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: LoftQ alternatively applies quantization and low-rank approximation to approximate pre-trained weights, providing an initialization that alleviates quantization discrepancy in LoRA fine-tuning.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: LoftQ initializes the network by jointly optimizing the initial values of the quantized backbone and low-rank adapters.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Alternating minimization avoids representation collapse.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: LoftQ achieves 88.0% accuracy on the MNLI-m dataset using 5 alternating steps.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: In QLoRA and LoftQ, 16-bit adapters cannot merge directly into 4-bit weights without dequantizing or suffering post-training quantization loss.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: Quantization-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation (QA-LoRA) resolves this tension by aligning degrees of freedom between quantization and adaptation.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: QA-LoRA uses group-wise operators to balance the degrees of freedom of quantization and adaptation, enabling low-rank adapters to be integrated into quantized weights.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: QA-LoRA enables the quantized base model and auxiliary low-rank weights to be integrated into an integer-quantized model without loss of accuracy.

section: Quantization Frontiers: Precision, Initialization, and Serving
text: This design eliminates runtime dequantization overhead during edge deployment.

section: Proposed Single-GPU Empirical Protocol
text: To evaluate these methods without conflating activations with adapter overhead, we specify a controlled benchmark on a 24 GB GPU (NVIDIA RTX 4090 or A10G) adapting LLaMA-3-8B on Alpaca (52k samples).

section: Proposed Single-GPU Empirical Protocol
text: The primary baseline is 16-bit LoRA (r=16, =32 across all linear projections), evaluated alongside DoRA (detached norm), QLoRA (NF4 base), LoftQ (4-bit initialized), QA-LoRA (INT4 group-wise), and an out-of-memory full fine-tuning reference.

section: Proposed Single-GPU Empirical Protocol
text: Controls: Random seeds are fixed to 42 across Python, NumPy, and PyTorch CUDA (torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True).

section: Proposed Single-GPU Empirical Protocol
text: We fix micro-batch size to B = 2, gradient accumulation to 8 (effective batch 16), gradient checkpointing enabled, AdamW (lr = 2 × 10-4), and contexts L \1024, 2048\.

section: Proposed Single-GPU Empirical Protocol
text: VRAM Profiling: Memory components are isolated via staged PyTorch tracking: (1) static weights M weights via memory_allocated() post-loading; (2) static optimizer buffers M opt after AdamW initialization, giving M static = M weights + M opt; (3) dynamic activation memory M act = M peak - M static via reset_peak_memory_stats() before the forward pass.

text: The scaling delta M act / L extracts the marginal activation cost per token.

section: Limitations, Unverified Claims, and Literature Scope
text: Rigorous empirical analysis requires acknowledging unverified claims and methodological limits.

section: Limitations, Unverified Claims, and Literature Scope
text: A pilot method developed in our laboratory reportedly halves training memory compared with LoRA.

section: Limitations, Unverified Claims, and Literature Scope
text: We designate this statement as strictly unverified: no empirical measurements, hardware details, batching schedules, or activation checkpointing specifications were supplied.

section: Limitations, Unverified Claims, and Literature Scope
text: Memory reductions measured during 175B model training with Adam cannot be transferred directly to consumer 7B or 8B model fine-tuning with activation caching under different batch configurations without empirical verification.

section: Limitations, Unverified Claims, and Literature Scope
text: On smaller models, base weights represent a smaller fraction of peak memory, dampening overall VRAM percentage savings when activation tensors dominate.

text: Additionally, QLoRA's throughput penalty during training dequantization and QA-LoRA's reliance on custom quantized kernels represent practical trade-offs rarely captured by parameter counts alone.
